quests.title: Strays on the Plain
quests.description:
Magra Dustwalker. Stand on this side of me - the herd's nervous and they'll shy off a stranger's shadow before they'll shy off mine.

I've run kodo north of the Crossroads for twenty years.

It has never been this bad, and I've said that out loud exactly twice, both times this season.

The hyenas have learned something. That's the part that frightens me, not the teeth.

They've worked out that a calf separated from the herd is a calf that does not come home - and so they don't attack. They shadow us. At a distance, all day, patient as a debt collector, and they take whatever lags.

Nothing taught them that. They arrived at it.

Look out over the plain. Brown-grey, spotted, grinning.

They will not run from you. They've never once had a reason to.
quests.accept_text: Out on the plain, shadowing the herd. They won't run.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's quieter.

Kodo don't flinch when something's after them - they just stop eating. Nobody tells you that.

They're eating again.

Come back when you've got your breath. There's a bigger problem, and it's in the sky.

quests.title: Thunder on the Wing
quests.description:
Something's been coming down on the herd out of a clear sky.

Plains thunderhawks. They hunt in pairs, they leave the calves scorched, and afterward the air smells like a storm that never arrived.

My kodo don't spook at much. I've walked this herd through a grass fire.

They spook at that.

So I want the hawks thinned, and I want flight-feathers brought back - pinions, the long ones off the big birds.

A thunderhawk pinion on a herd-bell keeps the others off. My grandmother did it, her mother did it, and I've never heard anyone explain why it works.

It works. I've got twenty years of herd to set against anyone who wants to argue.

You'll know the big ones by the crackle.

And watch your hair. It'll stand up before you see anything.
quests.accept_text: Off the plains thunderhawks over the herd. You'll know them by the crackle.
quests.turn_in_text:
Look at that. Still sparking.

These'll be on the herd-bells by dusk.

Come to me when you're tired of birds. There's a grey mesa east of here that wants a visit.

quests.title: Stingers at the Sentinels
quests.description:
The Sentinel Rocks - the sandstone teeth out north-west of the Crossroads.

Best shelter on these plains. The only shade a herd can lie down in between here and the hills, and every herder I've ever known has used it.

No kodo has slept there in three weeks.

Redstone scorpids have taken the crevices. That alone I could work around - you move the herd, you lose a season, you don't lose animals.

But something bigger has taken the scorpids.

I've been up close enough to see how they're behaving and they're not holding that ground for themselves. There's a brood-queen in those rocks and they're hers.

Red-brown, the size of a dog, tail like a sickle.

And the big mother, if she shows her face.

She will. They always do, once you've made a mess of the nursery.
quests.accept_text: The Sentinel Rocks, north-west of the Crossroads. In the crevices.
quests.turn_in_text:
Quiet in the rocks? Good.

My herd will be glad of that shade and so will my knees.

You've earned more than thanks.

quests.title: Old Sunhide
quests.description:
Every herder's story has a villain in it. I'd like to be honest with you about mine before you go.

Old Sunhide is a bull giraffe the height of a watchtower, with a hide exactly the colour of the dry grass he stands in.

He doesn't hunt. He's never killed anything in his life and he wouldn't know how.

He wanders. And wherever he wanders, calves end up flat, because a thing that size does not look down and a calf does not look up.

So I don't hold it against him. Not exactly. He hasn't done anything a giraffe shouldn't do.

I'm just tired of burying calves, and I've reached the age where tired is enough of a reason.

He walks the plain between here and the Crossroads. You'll see him a long way off - and you'll want to, because nothing that size should be able to come up on you quietly, and he can.

Thin his herd first, to take the cover away. Then him.
quests.accept_text: On the plain between here and the Crossroads. Thin his herd first.
quests.turn_in_text:
Gone?

... Good.

I won't say I'm not sorry. He was a good giraffe, in his way, and he never meant a thing by any of it.

Take these. They were my father's, and he'd have wanted them used rather than kept.

quests.title: Where the Herd Goes to Die
quests.description:
East of the Sentinel Rocks the plain rises into a shallow bowl.

The kodo have always walked into it when it was their time. Not driven. They go.

I've made that walk with three herds. You go in with them, you stand at the lip, and you come back on your own, and that is the oldest arrangement my people have with those animals.

It isn't quiet in there anymore.

The dead don't stay dead. I've watched a cow I knew the name of get up, and I've had a long time to decide how I feel about that and I haven't managed it.

And the vultures have gotten bold, which tells you how long it's been wrong.

Walk in. Look around. Come back out.

And put down what the bowl's still holding - the wraiths first, then the big horned one, if he's still wandering.

Kodo are not meant to come back.
quests.accept_text: The bowl east of the Sentinel Rocks. Wraiths first, then the horned one.
quests.turn_in_text:
Kodo are not meant to come back.

Every one you put down is a favour, and they'd know it if they could.

Take this, from the old herd.

quests.title: Smoke on the Horizon
quests.description:
Plainswatcher Dorn. Don't come up on the ridge from that side, you'll be against the sky.

I can see a sandstorm coming an hour out. That's not a boast, it's the job, and after eleven years it's most of what I am.

What I can't see is why the smoke over the Kolkar outpost has turned from brown to black.

Brown is cook-fires and tents. Black is something else being burned, deliberately, in quantity.

And a man on a ridge can only learn so much. I've been up here with a glass for four days turning it over, and all I've done is invent three answers I can't tell apart.

So somebody has to walk down there and look.

Follow the east road from the Crossroads until it forks off into trampled grass. That's them.

Look. Don't fight.

Come back and tell me what you actually saw - not what you think it means. I'll do the meaning.
quests.accept_text: East road from the Crossroads, where it forks into trampled grass.
quests.turn_in_text:
Twenty tents, a watchtower and a war-drum.

That's more than they had last season.

The centaur are building, which means they intend to keep it. Next job's louder.

quests.title: Taking the Outpost
quests.description:
That outpost is a way-station. Tents, a hitching line, and a great deal of centaur with spears.

It's where their war-parties stop, water, and go on - which makes it less a fort than a joint, and a joint is a thing you can hurt.

I want it hurt.

Here's the structure, because it matters to the order you do this in. The drudges carry the supplies. The taskmasters keep the drudges moving.

Take the taskmasters out and the drudges don't carry. Take the drudges out and the taskmasters have nothing to drive. Either way the way-station stops being a way to anywhere.

Drudges are the ones with clubs and no ambition.

Taskmasters are the ones with whips and plenty of it.

Come back with your armour a little dented. I'd be suspicious otherwise.
quests.accept_text: At the Kolkar outpost, east along the road. Drudges and the taskmasters driving them.
quests.turn_in_text:
That did something.

I could hear their drum change tempo from up here - actually change, mid-beat.

They don't like being surprised. Good. Let's make them dislike it more.

quests.title: Windseers' Whispers
quests.description:
The Kolkar windseers read the sky for their warlords.

And the sky has been telling them something about the Crossroads, because they've been reading it in the same direction for a month and that direction is us.

I can't read the sky. Eleven years out here and I can tell you what weather's coming and nothing at all about what it means.

What I can read is a stolen bundle of bone and kodo-hair, if somebody brings me one while it's still twitching.

The windseers carry them. So do the stormers - on the belt, the way a mother carries a purse, which is to say close and without thinking about it.

Bring me a few. One bundle is a mood. Several is an intention.

And don't look into one too long.

It looks back. I'd rather say that plainly than have you find out holding it.
quests.accept_text: Off the Kolkar windseers and stormers at the outpost.
quests.turn_in_text:
Hm.

That's not a prayer. That's a map.

And the map has a war-camp on it, east of here, with a cross through the Crossroads.

I'll want a closer look at that camp.

quests.title: The War Camp
quests.description:
The cross on that map leads east, past the Kodo Graveyard, deep into the plains.

There's a war camp out there and I have never been close to it.

I want to be straight with you about why, because you're about to go and I'd rather not be the man who sent you out on an errand he dressed up. It's not nerve. It's that a watcher who goes close stops being a watcher, and this ridge has been the Crossroads' early warning for eleven years.

I need three things and I need them counted, not estimated.

How many tents. How many marauders. And how bad that drum sounds from close range - because I've been hearing it at distance for a season and distance flatters a drum.

Take a few of them down before you leave. I want them to know somebody was there.

Marauders are on the outside. If you're running past marauders, you're already too deep.
quests.accept_text: East past the Kodo Graveyard, deep in the plains. Count the tents.
quests.turn_in_text:
A hundred tents. A hundred!

And a banner I haven't seen in years. Gorrak's.

That old war-chief is back and he's mustering. We cut the head off, or we pay for it later at a price somebody else sets.

quests.title: The Warbringer
quests.description:
Warbringer Gorrak has led march after march on the Crossroads.

Each one left that wall a little shorter than it was. Not breached - shorter. They take a course of stone and some people and they go, and the Crossroads rebuilds it slightly lower each time because that's what the stone and the season allow.

I've measured it. It's eleven years of measuring and it is the single most depressing figure I own.

He's old, he's huge, and he does not retreat. I've watched him hold ground that no commander should hold and be right about it twice.

I'm not going to ask you to do this for glory.

I'm asking because the next march is already in that drum, and I can hear what tempo it's on.

He rides the camp's edge when the drum starts.

Break the taskmasters first - they're what keeps that herd in a line. Then him. Quick and hard.
quests.accept_text: The edge of the war camp when the drum starts. Taskmasters first.
quests.turn_in_text:
It's quiet.

First time in three years I can hear the wind and nothing underneath it.

Take this. The Crossroads owes you a debt it will never once think to repay.

quests.title: Pests in the Furrows
quests.description:
Kranal Fiss. Mind the furrow, that's next year you're standing in.

I've farmed Grol'dom since before Orgrimmar had proper walls. Quilboar press me from two sides most seasons and I've made my arrangements with that - you plant more than you need and you accept what the year takes.

This season's problem is smaller and sneakier, and it's worse.

Poachers. Working the farm after dark. Lifting sacks, cutting traces, and laughing over the wall on their way out.

It's the laughing.

I've lost crops to quilboar, to drought and to one genuinely stupid decision about drainage, and none of it ever kept me awake. A thing that takes your grain and enjoys it is a different animal.

They hide in the furrows. Small men the colour of dirt.

Clear them out and I'll sleep through the night for the first time in a month.
quests.accept_text: In the furrows at Grol'dom Farm, after dark.
quests.turn_in_text:
It's been quiet since last night.

Not one laugh. Not one.

That's better than gold. Now - the sacks.

quests.title: Next Season's Seed
quests.description:
They took more than coin. I didn't realise for two days and I've been sick about it since.

They took the seed.

Next year's whole crop, in sacks, and I want you to understand that a farm is not the field. The field is dirt. The farm is what's in those sacks.

And they can't sell it on, which is the one piece of luck in this. Every sack is stamped with my mark - my father's mark, actually, and his father cut the stamp.

So they're either hoarding them or they're breaking the stamp off, and I've not let myself think too long about which.

The poachers carry them like pack-rats, and they've the habit of dropping them the moment a fight starts.

Don't tear the burlap.

I mean that. The burlap's got the only copy of next year written on it.
quests.accept_text: Off the poachers working the farm. Don't tear the burlap.
quests.turn_in_text:
They're all here. Every one, and the burlap isn't even torn.

You've saved a season, friend. I'll not forget which one.

quests.title: The Looter-Chief
quests.description:
Every gang has a chief, and this one's a brute called Bazz.

He doesn't work the fields. I've watched him for three nights now from the barn roof and he has not once bent his back - he stands at the wall and he runs the ones who do.

And he wields a stolen pitchfork like it owes him money.

It's mine. The tines are bent - I bent them, on a rock, the first spring I worked this ground, and I never straightened them because it still turned the earth fine.

I'd know it at two hundred paces and I have.

I'd like him gone. And I'd like the pitchfork back, and I'm aware those are two different sizes of request coming out of the same mouth.

His crew first. They keep the field between you and him and they're good at it.
quests.accept_text: At the farm wall with his crew. Big, loud, carrying a bent pitchfork.
quests.turn_in_text:
You took the pitchfork back? Hah!

... Still bent.

Never mind. Keep it. The farm is quiet, and that was always the prize.

quests.title: Choking the Oasis
quests.description:
Waterkeeper Sanu Goldenhoof. Drink first. You've come up the road and there's no sense talking thirsty.

Lushwater has been the first drink on the road to the Wailing Caverns for as long as my people have had a road. Not the best water in the Barrens. The first, which is a different thing and the more important one.

I keep it that way. That's the whole of my office.

This season the silithid came up out of the south dunes in a tide of chitin, and they are fouling the reeds.

Swarmers in the grass, creepers down in the reeds themselves.

And they are not here to drink. I want that understood, because it changes what this is. A thirsty thing you can share with. These have come to breed, and a pool with silithid breeding in it stops being a pool within a season.

Cut them back before it goes brown.

I cannot do it alone and I have spent a month establishing that.
quests.accept_text: In the grass and reeds around Lushwater Oasis.
quests.turn_in_text:
The water runs clear again. The Earth Mother will notice.

The silithid are patient, however. I will need you again, and I'd rather say so now than pretend otherwise.

quests.title: Vine-Choked Springs
quests.description:
The springs here are fed from below, and the thing that feeds them has started growing.

Tangle-vines. They've strangled the east spring until it no longer reaches the surface at all - and that spring ran through my mother's whole life and most of mine.

So they must be cut back. That part is simple and I take no pleasure in it.

But I want their hearts, and that part is not destruction.

A tangle-vine heart, taken whole and planted in clear soil, becomes a reed bed. Not a vine - a reed bed. The same thing that is choking the east spring will filter the west one if you put it somewhere it has room.

There is a lesson in that which I have been chewing on for forty years.

They hang on the north shore. Thick as a leg and quiet as a prayer until you step too close.

Bring the hearts whole.

And don't let them take your boots. They will try.
quests.accept_text: The north shore of the oasis. Bring the hearts whole.
quests.turn_in_text:
These will grow where I plant them, and the spring will drink again.

You've done something small and enormous at the same time. Most work is one or the other.

quests.title: The Queen of Lushwater
quests.description:
Every swarm has a mother.

This one is Queen Skitterwing, and she rules from a nest in the north reeds - the size of a horse, with wings that hum a note you feel in your teeth before you hear it.

I will say this once and then we will not discuss it again.

I do not harm anything needlessly. I have kept this water forty years and in that time I have killed what I had to and nothing beyond it, and I have turned down work that asked for more.

I am making an exception.

She will fill this oasis with her own children until there is no oasis, and she is not capable of choosing otherwise, and neither of those facts changes what has to be done.

The creepers guard the north reeds. She's behind them.

Do it cleanly. Don't linger.

Her song is not a lullaby, whatever it sounds like at the start.
quests.accept_text: The nest in the north reeds, behind the creepers.
quests.turn_in_text:
The reeds are silent.

Not the silence of death. The silence of rest - there is a difference and I have spent a lifetime learning to hear it.

Thank you, friend of the oasis. Take what the pool has to give.

quests.title: The Forgotten Pilgrims
quests.description:
Torga. Shrine's behind me - don't mind the water, it's always that colour at this hour.

The Forgotten Pools were a place of pilgrimage once. A chain of sacred springs on the long walk between Orgrimmar and the south, and people came here for a hundred years.

The pilgrims never stopped coming.

They stopped leaving.

I keep the shrine and I watch over the dead, and those are supposed to be two jobs. Here they've collapsed into one.

They wander the water's edge in robes that haven't been dry in decades.

And they carry prayer beads - every one of them, still on the wrist, which after this long is its own kind of statement.

The beads hold the name of whoever owned them. Bring me some and I'll read them back.

I want to know who they were. That's the whole of it. Somebody should and there's nobody else here.
quests.accept_text: Along the water's edge at the Forgotten Pools. They still wear the beads.
quests.turn_in_text:
Six names.

Six people who walked all this way because they believed in something, and not one of them has been said out loud in forty years.

We'll carry the beads to Orgrimmar's shrine. They've earned that much.

quests.title: Murk in the Water
quests.description:
The murlocs came up the old river after the pilgrims stopped coming.

I've thought about that order of events more than is healthy. They didn't drive anyone out. They moved into a place that had already been given up on, which is what murlocs do and what I'd do.

They fish the pools. They foul the springs.

And they have started building something on the east bank that looks a very great deal like a shrine of their own.

I am not a violent woman. I came here to tend a stone and read names.

I am, however, extremely tired of explaining myself to a fish.

The pool murlocs are the ones on the shore. The flesheaters are the ones that have been down in the deep too long, and you'll know which is which immediately.

Be careful of those. They bite, and they don't stop at the first one.
quests.accept_text: The shore and deep water of the Forgotten Pools.
quests.turn_in_text:
Clear water. Well. Clearer.

Take this. It was a gift from a pilgrim and I'm not one for heirlooms.

quests.title: Maeve the Weeping
quests.description:
One of them never stopped walking.

Maeve. The others drift - they go where the water takes them and they've no direction in it at all. She walks. South pool, same circuit, every dusk, and she has been doing it longer than anyone here was alive.

In a wedding veil.

She sings something nobody remembers the words to, and the pool-water comes after her like a train, and the first time I saw it I stood in the reeds for an hour and did nothing.

She isn't malicious. I need you to go in knowing that, because what you'll meet won't behave like it.

She's very, very sad, and sadness has teeth when it's had this long.

Do what you must. Be gentle about it.

She doesn't know she's dead.

That's all the sorrow there is in this, right there in that one sentence.
quests.accept_text: The south pool at dusk. Be gentle about it.
quests.turn_in_text:
I heard her stop.

I'll read her prayer at dawn - properly, with the name off the beads, which I have now.

Take this. She'd have wanted somebody to carry it on.

quests.title: The Drowned Warlord
quests.description:
Gaharrz is not a murloc. Not exactly, and I've had to build the sentence carefully.

He's what happens when a murloc warlord drowns in a sacred pool and refuses to be finished with it.

The water here was meant to do something to the dead. That was the entire point of the pilgrimage - people walked a month to be laid in it. And whatever it was meant to do, it did to him, and he was the wrong thing to do it to.

He's the reason the shrine goes quiet at dusk. Not the murlocs. Him.

And he's the reason I keep one hand near a cleaver at night, which is not how a shrine-keeper is supposed to sleep.

He lives in the middle pool.

The elementals guard him - and you should know before you raise a hand to them that they were pool spirits once, and they didn't choose this either.

Kill them, then him. It's the only way this shrine sleeps.
quests.accept_text: The middle pool. The elementals stand between you and him.
quests.turn_in_text:
The pool's still.

First time since I came here. I keep looking at it.

I'll light a lamp for you at the shrine. Take this, from the dead.

quests.title: Mourning at the Shrine
quests.description:
Keeper Ahnmar. Walk slowly past the stone - not out of ceremony, it's uneven and people turn an ankle.

The Shrine of the Fallen Warrior marks where a champion of the plains died holding a pass against a war-party three times his number.

He held it. That's the thing worth saying and the thing people forget to - the pass held, and everybody behind it walked home.

I tend the stone. Forty years, and it has been quiet work and good work.

Lately the stone is not alone.

Mourning spirits drift in at dusk and will not leave, and the sound they make is very hard to bear. I've stopped sleeping within hearing of it, which means I've stopped sleeping at the shrine, which means I'm not doing the job.

They gather round the stone at sunset.

They don't mean harm. They simply cannot stop weeping.

Release them. Be kind about it - that's not a flourish, it's the instruction.
quests.accept_text: Around the shrine stone at sunset.
quests.turn_in_text:
The shrine is quiet.

That is the most sacred sound it knows, and I'd forgotten.

Thank you for your gentleness.

quests.title: The Echo of the Fallen Warrior
quests.description:
The warrior who died here did not go quietly, and something of him is still at this stone.

Not a ghost. I want to be precise, because I've had people come out here expecting a ghost and handle it wrongly.

An echo. A memory of the fight, replaying itself for anyone who walks into it - the same movements, the same order, the same end.

He isn't haunting the shrine. He's still in the pass.

I believe he's caught. And I believe he cannot leave until somebody shows him the battle is over, because nothing out here has ever told him, and the one thing a man holding a pass cannot do is stop.

Face him as an equal. He'll not stop for words - he can't, he isn't hearing you yet.

And when he falls, tell him the pass held.

That's all. That's the entire thing he needs and it's one sentence.
quests.accept_text: At the shrine stone. Face him as an equal - and when he falls, tell him.
quests.turn_in_text:
The pass held. I told him.

He... nodded.

[Ahnmar is a while saying anything else.]

Take this. It belongs to the warrior, and he'd want it carried by somebody who understood what it was for.

quests.title: Toll Collectors
quests.description:
Dogan Ironcart. Raider's Rest is mine - I've run this waystation since the Crossroads was a hitching post and a rumour.

I pay my taxes. To the right people, on time, in full, and I'd invite an audit if anyone out here could read.

Somebody else has started collecting on the south road.

They call themselves toll-men. I'll give them the word - it's a better word than bandit and it's done them a lot of good with drivers who want to believe a payment ends the conversation.

It doesn't. They leave nobody with change.

That's the detail that tells you what they are. A toll is a price. These men take the purse.

Outriders work the road. Cutthroats wait in the oasis grass, which is where the real business happens.

I'll pay the difference out of my own pocket, and gladly, because I have done the arithmetic on a closed south road and it is considerably worse.
quests.accept_text: Outriders on the south road, cutthroats in the oasis grass.
quests.turn_in_text:
The roads run smoother already. You can feel it in the cart-wheels before you hear it anywhere else.

Business is a state of mind, friend.

And my mind is a good deal calmer this morning.

quests.title: Dogan's Missing Powder
quests.description:
A shipment of blasting powder went missing on the south road. Mine, insured, and the insurance is a separate tragedy I won't trouble you with.

The bandits have found a use for it.

They've got bombardiers now - and they've been lobbing kegs at passing wagons, which is not robbery. You cannot rob a wagon you've blown apart. There's nothing left worth carrying off.

So somebody out there is doing it for the enjoyment of the thing, and that changes my estimate of everything else they've done this year.

I want the kegs back. Intact.

Before they work out a reliable way to light them, because at the moment they are extremely bad at it and that is the only reason this road still has wagons on it.

They carry them in satchels on the back. Small kegs, long fuses.

Cut the fuses first. And bring them to me preferably not on fire.
quests.accept_text: Off the bandit bombardiers on the south road. Cut the fuses first.
quests.turn_in_text:
Four kegs, no fuses lit.

You may be the most careful soul in the Barrens. That's an excellent quality in a merchant.

Pity about the pay.

quests.title: The Crocolisk Problem
quests.description:
Raider's Rest has water. That's the whole reason it exists and the whole reason it's a problem.

Where there's water, there are things that want you in it.

The watering-hole crocolisks have taken three oxen this season and one of my best guards. I'll say his name if you want it, but I've noticed I've started listing him after the oxen and I don't love what that says.

And the smugglers on the shore have been feeding them.

Not to keep them off. Not for any arrangement I can find a motive in.

For fun. I've watched it from the porch with a glass - a man stood there throwing meat into the shallows and laughing, in a place where he keeps his own boat.

So I'd like both gone, and I'd like them gone in the same afternoon.

Crocs in the shallows. Smugglers on the shore. Fewer of both would be a considerable improvement to my year.
quests.accept_text: The shallows and shore at Raider's Rest.
quests.turn_in_text:
Quiet shore, and the oxen are safe.

You've the thanks of a very tired merchant, which is worth more than it sounds.

quests.title: Quickfinger
quests.description:
The smugglers have a captain and the captain has a name. Silas Quickfinger.

Two years. He is, by my own books, the single most expensive man on the south road - more than the bandits, more than the crocs, more than the year we lost the bridge.

And he has never once been caught holding anything.

I want you to appreciate that properly, because it's not luck. Three separate sets of guards have taken that man and searched him and found a clean pair of hands, and every time, the cargo was already gone.

Somebody taught him. I've stopped speculating about who.

I have finally had enough, and I'll admit the timing is personal rather than commercial.

He runs the oasis-island camp.

You'll know him by the lack of anything in his hands.

Check your pockets before. And after.
quests.accept_text: The oasis-island camp. He's the one holding nothing.
quests.turn_in_text:
You found the ledger?

... That's an enormous help.

I'd hoped you wouldn't touch it. I'd hoped for a great many things this year.

Take the reward. You've earned every coin of it.

quests.title: The Dreadmist Approach
quests.description:
Scout Zarla. Get down off the skyline first - no, properly down, those cliffs carry sound.

Dreadmist Peak is the grey massif in the north-west corner of the plain, and the cultists inside it have been very quiet lately.

I want to be clear that quiet is the problem.

I've watched that approach for a week. When they're raiding, there's traffic - runners out, carts in, a certain amount of shouting about rope. I know what a busy cult looks like.

There's been almost nothing for six days, and the few that do come out are walking in step.

A cult that's stopped doing things has finished preparing to do one thing.

Follow the road past the third baobab, up to where the cliffs close in. Their banners hang at the canyon mouth.

Look. Don't linger.

And don't touch the banners. I'll explain why when you're back, if I turn out to be right.
quests.accept_text: Past the third baobab, up to the canyon mouth. Don't touch the banners.
quests.turn_in_text:
A ring of red banners and a summoning circle at the mouth.

That's not a cult anymore. That's a ritual site.

Something's coming through, and soon.

quests.title: Imps in the Brush
quests.description:
They've been summoning imps. Small, sharp, giggly things that spill out of that canyon and bother everything in the brush.

I'd normally leave them. They're a nuisance, not a threat, and chasing nuisances is how a scout stops noticing threats.

But an imp is a symptom, and symptoms can be read.

I want one cut open.

Because whatever they're feeding those things is coming out of that canyon too, and I would rather learn what it is from an imp than from the thing the imps are practice for.

The heart's about the size of a plum, and it smoulders - it'll still be warm in your bag at dusk, which is how I know they're not feeding them anything ordinary.

Wear gloves. Not a suggestion.

And don't let it giggle at you. They do that after. I've no explanation and I've stopped asking for one.
quests.accept_text: Off the imps in the brush below the canyon. Wear gloves.
quests.turn_in_text:
Hm. Brimstone and blood.

They've been feeding the imps on something that was not an animal.

I'll send word to the Warchief. Take this.

quests.title: Veshra the Voidcaller
quests.description:
Veshra is their field commander, and she is the reason that circle is going up on schedule.

A voidcaller. Smile like a razor, and a list - an actual written list - of things she has summoned, which I have seen through a glass and have not been able to stop thinking about since.

She's stationed at the canyon mouth supervising the work.

Not casting. Supervising. Walking the circle, correcting people, sending things back to be redone.

That's what makes her the target rather than the ritual itself. The circle is stone and paint and anybody can lay stone. She's the one who knows whether it's right.

If she falls, it falters.

The cultists around the circle feed her power, so take them first - and then her, before anybody else there works out what the correct order is.
quests.accept_text: At the ritual circle, canyon mouth of Dreadmist. Cultists first.
quests.turn_in_text:
The ritual faltered. I felt it from the ridge.

Something snapped, and the whole canyon went quiet in a way it hasn't been all week.

Take this. Well earned.

quests.title: Quills and Barbs
quests.description:
Ranger Kishi. Don't sit on that stump, I've not checked it since yesterday.

The Razormane at Bramblescar have a new weapon and I'd like somebody competent to look at it.

Quill-throwers. They hurl poison-barbed quills out of the thorn thickets, from cover, at range.

That's new. Quilboar have always fought the same way - straight at you and loudly, which is awful and at least legible.

Somebody down there has had an idea.

I've been stuck three times. Three. The third one I didn't see coming at all and I've been doing this eleven years.

I want a bundle of the quills for study, and I want it collected by somebody who isn't already carrying three doses of whatever that is.

The quillthrowers and the veterans carry them.

Handle them by the string. The poison is still wet on them - and it is not a good wet, it's the other kind.
quests.accept_text: Off the quillthrowers and veterans at Bramblescar. Handle them by the string.
quests.turn_in_text:
Now that's careful work.

I'll send these to the Apothecaries. They can build an antidote off a wet sample and not off a dry one.

Take this. And please wash your hands.

quests.title: Tusks of the Battleboar
quests.description:
Across the road the Bristleback keep a different kind of weapon.

Battleboars. Trained to charge anything on two legs, and - this is the part I need proving - bred angrier every generation.

That's my claim and nobody above me believes it. A found boar is a nuisance. A bred boar is a programme, and a programme means somebody has a plan that runs past this season.

So I need tusks.

A wild boar's tusk and a fourth-generation war-boar's tusk do not look the same, and I can put the two on a table in front of a sceptical orc and win the argument in about four seconds.

And I want the briarweavers silenced while you're in there.

They're what keeps those boars calm. The boars won't be calm without them, which is unpleasant for about a minute and solves the problem for a year.
quests.accept_text: At the Bristleback camp across the road. Tusks off the boars, and the weavers who keep them.
quests.turn_in_text:
That's the evidence.

The Bristleback are breeding a war-herd, and now the Warchief will know it from a tusk instead of from a ranger with a theory.

Take your payment and my thanks.

quests.title: The Wardchief of Bramblescar
quests.description:
Wardchief Thulg commands the Razormane at Bramblescar from a thorn-throne at the camp's heart, and I want to be careful about how I describe him.

He's clever. Properly clever - the quill-throwers are his, and so is the way they're deployed, and neither of those is something a quilboar camp arrives at by accident.

He's brutal, which is ordinary out here.

And he is entirely unburdened by doubt, which is the rare part and the dangerous one.

Here's my thinking, and you may disagree. This whole quilboar war runs on his command. The Bristleback have numbers and the Razormane have direction, and direction is the thing that's been making it a war instead of a feud.

A Razormane without a Wardchief is a Razormane without a war.

He sits at the heart of Bramblescar. The veterans hold the approach.

Cut through them - and finish him before he's up off that throne.
quests.accept_text: The heart of Bramblescar. The veterans hold the approach.
quests.turn_in_text:
The Razormane are leaderless.

That won't last. It never does. But it's a start and I haven't had one of those in a while.

Take this.

quests.title: The Sow-Mother of Agama'gor
quests.description:
Now the other side of the road, and I'd like to explain myself rather than just point.

The Bristleback have their own mother. Sow-Mother Grunka, the Brood-Matriarch, and she has sired half that war-herd personally.

I took Thulg from the Razormane. If I stop there, I haven't ended a war - I've picked a winner.

And a quilboar tribe that wins this war comes out of it with a herd, a grudge and nobody left to spend it on but us.

So both chiefs, or neither. Fairness is a rare luxury in a quilboar war and this is the one chance to afford it.

The camp at Agama'gor is a horror of mud and tusks. I've been to the edge of it once and I'd rather not describe the middle.

She sits in it.

Her raiders will try to stop you. Don't let them get set.
quests.accept_text: The Bristleback camp at Agama'gor, across the road. She sits in the middle.
quests.turn_in_text:
Both chiefs gone. The war will stumble now.

It was never going to be quiet. It will be quieter, and out here that's the whole of what anybody gets.

quests.title: Snapper Season
quests.description:
Bridgewarden Karga. Walk on the left-hand planks, the right ones are next week's job.

This bridge connects Durotar to the Barrens. There isn't another one. Everything that moves between the two goes over my planks, and when it doesn't, people go round by the ford and some of them don't come back.

I keep the planks sound and the traffic moving. That's the whole office and I'm the only one in it.

The riverbank snappers have taken to chewing the pilings.

Not the rails. Not the deck. The pilings - underwater, where I can't see them, and I only found out because a piling I'd never worried about went soft under a boot-heel.

I need shell plates to armour the supports.

Snappers on the bank, shells like shields. Bring me plates and I'll nail them to the pilings tonight.

Let the next snapper try chewing that.
quests.accept_text: The riverbank either side of the Southfury bridge.
quests.turn_in_text:
Plates thick as slabs.

This bridge will outlast us all now, which was the aim.

Take this.

quests.title: Bridge Watch
quests.description:
Pilings are armoured. So now it's the sky and the shore, which is a bridge-warden's life in one sentence.

Sunscale screechers have taken to dive-bombing travellers at the Barrens end.

They're not hunting. They're not big enough to carry anybody off and they know it. They do it to move people along, and it works - I've watched four drivers break into a run on a bridge, which is exactly how you lose a cart over the side.

And the snappers have not learned their lesson. I'd hoped. I'd actually hoped.

Next caravan crosses in two days and I'd like the bank clear before it does, because a caravan that has a bad crossing takes the ford next time and tells everyone to.

Screechers from above, snappers from below.

I'll pay you in coin and curses, and the curses are free.
quests.accept_text: The Barrens end of the bridge - the air above and the bank below.
quests.turn_in_text:
Quiet at last! Caravans can cross in peace.

Take this - and think of me kindly when you cross.

quests.title: The Mouth of the Wailing
quests.description:
Now I will tell you where the water actually comes from, and then you'll understand why I've been asking you for all of it.

The Wailing Caverns are this oasis's other half.

Every spring at Lushwater is fed from the green warren beneath it. Not near it. Beneath - the same water, a day earlier.

And for a season something down in that warren has been dreaming wrong.

The pools run cold at dusk. Not cool. Cold, at the hour the day is warmest, and I have put my hands in that water every evening of my life.

And the animals come up out of the mouth already mad.

That's what I need you to hold on to down there. They're not wild. They're sick, and they were beautiful once, and every one of them was drinking the same water I was.

The mouth is south of the bluff. Raptors on the bank, pythons in the reeds, crocolisks where it's deepest.

Be quick. And don't take any of it personally.
quests.accept_text: The cavern mouth, south of the bluff.
quests.turn_in_text:
They were beautiful once, you know.

Come. There's more to understand and I'd rather you heard it from me than worked it out down there.

quests.title: Dewdrops of the Dream
quests.description:
Where the dreaming leaks out, it condenses. That's not a metaphor and I'd like a moment before you decide it is.

There's a dew in the mid-halls, on the wisps that drift through them.

It does not evaporate. I've had a bead of it in a dry clay cup on a hot shelf for eleven days and it is exactly the size it was.

And if you look into one, you see what the sleeper sees.

I've done that twice. The first time I learned more about this warren than in forty years of keeping its water. The second time I lost most of an afternoon and I've not done it since.

So: collect them, and do not stare into them.

I mean that kindly. I'm not warning you off a danger - I'm telling you what it costs, as somebody who paid it.

And clear the broodlings off the nests while you're in there. They'll be at your back otherwise.
quests.accept_text: The mid-halls of the warren, where the wisps drift. Don't stare into the dew.
quests.turn_in_text:
Five drops, and not one spilled.

Look at what it shows. No - look properly, once, and then put it down.

The sleeper is not alone. The Fang have his ear.

quests.title: The Fang Initiates
quests.description:
The Druids of the Fang were a school of healers.

I want to start there every time, and I've been corrected for it, and I'll keep doing it.

They are a cult now. That much is settled and I'm not arguing it.

But the cult has initiates who still believe they are healing - who came down here to learn the thing I learned, from people who were teaching it properly within my lifetime.

What I need is evidence that the school is one body. Not a scatter of lost druids. One hand, one seal, one instruction going out to all of them.

Because if it's a scatter, then it's a tragedy and we clear it out.

And if it's one hand, then somebody is doing this deliberately and there is a name at the end of the chain.

The initiates break a shard at the end of each rite. Bring me a few and I'll fit them together.

Don't linger to watch the rite. The druids are not kind about interruptions.
quests.accept_text: The west arm of the warren. Shards off the initiates, and the druids guarding them.
quests.turn_in_text:
Four shards. And they fit together.

One seal. One hand.

It's time to name the hand, and I find I've known it for a while.

quests.title: The Lady of the Fang
quests.description:
Lady Anacondra was my student.

Long ago. I taught her the water, and the way the warren feeds it, and how to tell a sick animal from an angry one - which is the first lesson and the one everything else sits on.

She was the first of the Fang to forget which was the lesson and which was the sickness.

I don't say that bitterly. I've had decades and I've got it down to a fact.

She keeps the north platform of the Serpentbloom Cavern now, and her druids hold the river crossing below it.

I'd ask you to end it gently.

[A pause.]

I know that isn't how it will go. I'm asking anyway, because I'd rather have asked.

The lashers grip at the river's edge. She waits above them.

And she will heal through anything you throw at her unless you move on her fast. She was always better at that than I was.
quests.accept_text: The north platform of the Serpentbloom Cavern, above the river crossing.
quests.turn_in_text:
She was clever, once. She could have been so much more than this.

Take this. It's what she was supposed to become.

quests.title: Lord Cobrahn and the Old Shell
quests.description:
Two of the warren's masters sit on the western ring and they are not the same kind of problem.

Lord Cobrahn has begun to prefer his serpent form. That's the phrase the Fang use and it's doing an enormous amount of work - what it means is that he has stopped coming back, and at some point he stopped intending to.

And then there's Kresh.

A river-turtle old enough to remember when this pool was a pool. I knew that animal before the Fang went wrong. I have fed it.

Kresh is not evil. Kresh is hurt.

I'm aware that will not matter in the slightest to the fight. It matters to me, and I'd like it said out loud before you go rather than after.

Cobrahn's in his den, west. Kresh is in the pool further north.

Kresh retreats into the shell and hits hard coming out - so don't crowd it when it closes.

Cobrahn's venom lingers. Bring something that cures.
quests.accept_text: The western ring - Cobrahn in his den, Kresh in the pool north of it.
quests.turn_in_text:
Both done. The west ring is quiet.

I did not expect to miss the sound of the old turtle shifting in the water.

I do.

quests.title: Thunder and Slumber
quests.description:
Two more, and then the ring can be walked in either direction, which it hasn't been in years.

Lord Pythas holds the east gallery with thunder and sleep.

Skum holds the north with thunder alone - an old lizard, and simpler for it.

They're not working together. I want that clear, because people go in expecting a pair and fight them like one. They've each taken an end and neither has crossed the middle in a season.

That's why both have to go. Take one and the ring is still shut; you've just changed which way round you can't walk it.

Pythas casts sleep, and a sleeping friend in that gallery is how parties end. Carry a trinket, or a friend who can wake you, and ideally both.

Skum's roar weakens your arms. It builds.

So kill him before it stacks - that fight gets harder the longer you are polite about it.
quests.accept_text: Pythas in the east gallery, Skum in the north.
quests.turn_in_text:
The ring's open.

The Fang's own gallery waits at the heart of it.

Be careful in there. It is quieter than it has any business being.

quests.title: The Everliving and the Serpent
quests.description:
At the heart of the ring, in the Chamber of the Fang, two things stand between you and the sleeper's door.

Lord Serpentis. The cult's last lord and by a distance its most devoted - the others drifted into this. He chose it, repeatedly, and he is still choosing it.

And Verdan the Everliving.

A thing of bark and root that the cult has been feeding for years. Feeding, not growing. There is a difference and you can see it in the shape of the thing - it did not get that way on water and light.

I don't know what they were feeding it. I have a guess and the guess involves the reed-cutters I've lost, and I am not going to say more than that to somebody about to walk in there.

Serpentis shields himself before every fight. Strip it with everything at once - patience is exactly wrong against him.

Verdan hits like a falling tree.

And don't stand in the vines. They're his and they're slower than he is.
quests.accept_text: The Chamber of the Fang, at the heart of the ring.
quests.turn_in_text:
Both lie still.

Behind them is the way into Naralex's Dream.

I wish I could go with you. I'd be no use and I'd slow you, and I've had a long time to be honest about that.

I'll wait here.

quests.title: Naralex's Dream
quests.description:
Naralex came here to wake the Barrens.

That was the whole of it. A green dream under a dry plain, and a druid who thought he could pull one up into the other, and I'd like it on the record that it was a good idea.

He fell asleep inside his own dream instead.

And the dream fed on him. Years of it, down there, with nobody able to reach him and the water coming up colder every season.

At its heart now waits Mutanus the Devourer. A nightmare wearing the shape of a murloc, which is the dream's own joke and not a kind one.

End it. Bring me the pearl.

And then the dream may go back to being a dream, and this oasis may go back to being fed by something that isn't in pain.

North through the Chamber, then west into the Dream.

Mutanus devours, and then it screams. The scream will hurt you worse than the bite.

Bring everyone you trust. All of them.
quests.accept_text: North through the Chamber of the Fang, then west into the Dream.
quests.turn_in_text:
The pearl is warm.

I can feel him in it. Sleeping - properly sleeping, for the first time in years.

Take this, with everything this oasis has to give. It's not a figure of speech. Ask for anything.

quests.title: Old Hissfang
quests.description:
One more thing, and it has nothing to do with the Fang or the dream, and I'd like that understood before you go in.

There's a python in the south hollow of the warren.

Older than the Fang. Older than the oasis, I think, though I can't prove the second one and I've tried.

It is not sick.

That's the whole distinction I'm drawing. Everything else you've put down in that warren was suffering and I asked you to end it. This one is simply large, and it is doing exactly what it has always done.

And it has been eating my reed-cutters for three seasons.

So I'm asking, politely, and without pretending it's mercy: stop it.

The south hollow, off the first cavern, west of the entry tube.

It is very large.

Do not be impressed. People are, and that is the moment it takes them.
quests.accept_text: The south hollow off the first cavern, west of the entry tube.
quests.turn_in_text:
Three seasons of missing reed-cutters, resolved.

Thank you.

It was a magnificent animal and I'd not have anyone say otherwise.
